title: Finite-type parameter scheme for fixed-degree divisors in a smooth open curve
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ be a closed immersion [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $C\to S$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $U\subset C$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $U\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix an integer $d\geq0$. The functor on $S$-schemes $T$ of closed subschemes $E\subset U_T=U\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product] finite locally free of rank $d$ over $T$ is represented by a scheme $V_d$ of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here finite locally free of rank $d$ means finite with pushforward of its structure sheaf locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus d}$. The universal $E_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset U\times_SV_d$ is also closed in $C\times_SV_d$ and is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_{V_d}/V_d$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. Its divisor line $\mathcal O(E_{\mathrm{univ}})$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] and this representing property commute with arbitrary base change of $S$. The scheme $V_d$ is an open subscheme of the projective Hilbert scheme of $C/S$ with constant Hilbert polynomial $d$ [def-sfb-projective-fibre-hilbert-polynomial].

source.place: Tag 0DPE, lemma-hilb-open; Tag 0DPI, lemma-hilb-qc-over-base, with the constant Hilbert polynomial d. Scheme representation and universal family: pic.tex Tag 0B9A (proposition-hilb-d-representable) and Tag 0B9B (remark-when-proposition-applies); Cartier property: Tag 0B9D (lemma-divisors-on-curves) on the smooth open, extended by the empty divisor outside the support. The projective Hilbert scheme is the existing lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] to the specified embedding of $C$ over the Noetherian base $S$. Let $H=H_d$ and $q:Z\to H$ be its universal closed family in $C_H$. Thus $H$ is projective, separated and of finite type over $S$, and $Z/H$ is flat and finitely presented with fibre polynomial $d$. Base-changing the embedding of $C$ gives a closed embedding of $C_H$ in $\mathbf P^n_H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and composing it with $Z\hookrightarrow C_H$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-hilbert-finite-locally-free] to this composite: $q$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. The theorem permits arbitrary bases, so its application does not require proving that $H$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0DPE (lemma-hilb-open), fixed-polynomial restriction; projective representation supplied by the cited existing node; numerical bridge as in the new node source

proof.text: Let $B=|Z|\setminus|Z\cap U_H|$, a closed subset of $Z$, and set $V=H\setminus q(B)$. The image $q(B)$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], so $V$ is open. To check its exact functorial meaning, take $h:T\to H$. For $t\in T$ a boundary point above $h(t)$ survives in $Z_T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]: the nonempty fibre over $h(t)$ maps surjectively to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h(t))$, and its base change to $\kappa(t)$ remains nonempty, also after restricting to any boundary point and its residue field. Conversely any boundary point of $Z_T$ projects to one above $h(t)$. Consequently $Z_T\subset U_T$ if and only if every $h(t)$ belongs to $V$, which is precisely factorization through the open subscheme $V$. This checks the support condition on arbitrary test schemes, including nonreduced ones; factorization through an open is determined by its underlying image.

source.place: Tag 0DPE (lemma-hilb-open), proof hint filled in by the closed-image complement and field-base-change argument; morphisms.tex Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective)

proof.text: For a test scheme $T/S$ and a closed $E\subset U_T$ finite locally free of rank $d$ in the statement's pushforward convention, [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and [lem-pc-flf-properties] identify this with finite locally free degree $d$. In the reverse conversion, on an affine base the algebra is finite free, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] supplies flatness and local finite presentation; the fibre dimensions are the ranks. The finite map $E\to T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. The target $C_T$ is separated over $T$: use projective-space properness [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] and properness of a closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], after base-changing the specified embedding. Hence $E\to C_T$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target]. It is also the given closed immersion into $U_T$ followed by an open immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion into $C_T$. Compose with $C_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$. The numerical bridge gives fibre polynomial $d$, and the representing property of $H_d$ gives a unique $h:T\to H$. Its family is supported in $U_T$, so Step 2 gives a unique factorization through $V$.

source.place: Tag 0DPE (lemma-hilb-open), first sentence of the proof hint; pic.tex Tag 0B9A (proposition-hilb-d-representable), functor of points

proof.text: Conversely a map $T\to V$ pulls back $Z$ to a closed subscheme of $U_T$ by Step 2, and [lem-pc-hilb-functorial] preserves finite locally free degree $d$. These constructions are inverse: both retain the very same ideal-defined closed subscheme, and uniqueness of the classifying map is part of the representing property of $H$. They are natural under pullback. Thus set $V_d=V$ and $E_{\mathrm{univ}}=Z_V$; in particular this universal family is already closed in $C_V$. For finite type, $H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The open immersion $V\to H$ is of finite presentation, hence finite type, by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation] (use the identity closed immersion of $V$). Composing with $H\to S$ gives finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0DPE (lemma-hilb-open), natural transformation and open locus; Tag 0DPI (lemma-hilb-qc-over-base), fixed-polynomial boundedness, here supplied by Noetherianity of the projective H_d

proof.text: The base change $U_V\to V$ is smooth of relative dimension one by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Apply the implication $(1)\Rightarrow(2)$ of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] to $E_{\mathrm{univ}}\subset U_V$. Its ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor there. On $C_V\setminus|E_{\mathrm{univ}}|$ its ideal is the unit ideal, generated by the non-zero-divisor $1$. These two opens cover $C_V$, since the support is contained in $U_V$. Therefore the ideal is effective Cartier everywhere on $C_V$. The map $E_{\mathrm{univ}}\to V$ is flat, so [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier] gives the relative assertion. Its ideal is invertible by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible], and its dual is the line $\mathcal O(E_{\mathrm{univ}})$ by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. No smoothness of $C_V$ away from $U_V$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0B9D (lemma-divisors-on-curves), (1) implies (2); divisors.tex definition of effective Cartier ideal and its local nature

proof.text: For any $S'\to S$, the base change $V_d\times_SS'$ represents the same functor on $S'$-schemes: the fibre-product identities identify $U_T$ and $C_T$ with their original versions, and [lem-pc-hilb-functorial] preserves the degree condition. The open Hilbert embedding and universal family are the pullbacks of those already constructed by the base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] and the factorization criterion of Step 2. This argument does not assume $S'$ Noetherian. Finally $C_V/V$ and $E_{\mathrm{univ}}/V$ are finitely presented: the former is a base change of the given finitely presented $C/S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and the latter is the universal Hilbert family. The latter is flat. Thus [lem-sfb-flat-closed-family-ideal-base-change] identifies the pulled-back ideal with the ideal of the pulled-back divisor. Dualizing commutes with pullback for an invertible ideal: on a trivializing open, a basis $e$ pulls back to $1\otimes e$, and its dual basis maps to the functional $1\otimes e\mapsto1$; on overlaps a unit transition $u$ changes both dual bases by $u^{-1}$. These local maps glue, proving the asserted base-change identification of $\mathcal O(E)$.

I checked moduli 0DPE (lemma-hilb-open and its proof hint), pic 0B9D lines 408-425 (implication (1)=>(2) needs no Noetherian or proper hypothesis) and more-morphisms 02LS (proper with finite fibres implies finite, over any base). Step 1: the projective Hilbert scheme H_d and the new bridge make q finite locally free over H without H being Noetherian. One unstated detail: the bridge needs Z->H quasi-compact and quasi-separated; this holds because Z is closed in the proper P^n_H. Step 2: I checked the open V = H minus q(B) on every test scheme. The image of Z_T in Z equals the preimage of h(T) because surjectivity survives base change, and the open-immersion definition then covers nonreduced T. Step 3: the two finite-locally-free conventions convert into each other. E is closed in C_T because a proper map to a separated target is proper and a proper immersion is closed. Step 4: the two maps are inverse; V->H is finitely presented because H is Noetherian, so V is of finite type over S. Step 5: E_univ is Cartier on U_V by 0B9D, its ideal is the unit ideal off its support, and the two opens cover C_V. Step 6: base change in S needs no Noetherian S'; the pulled-back ideal is the ideal of the pulled-back divisor because C_V/V is finitely presented and E/V is flat and finitely presented; the dual line is computed explicitly. New node lem-sfb-constant-hilbert-finite-locally-free: true (zero-dimensional fibres, 02LS, then 02KB, then h^0 = d; d=0 gives Z empty), statement-only, its objects introduced, strictly smaller than the item. No duplicate: I ran my own search of DAG statements and blueprint_refs, and lem-pc-hilb-representable (0B9A) gives neither the open-in-H_d clause nor finite type. Batch 5: lem-trf-structural-fibrewise-open-locality is a generic Zariski-locality lemma for flatness, finite presentation and closed immersions, and is no part of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality assumptions or their proofs, so it is not a RETURN. The declared tool_uses are generic scheme lemmas and are accepted. No SGA citation. No changes.
